articles.title: AI Destruction Isn’t Hypothetical. It’s Already Here.
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: We’re several weeks into a fierce debate over whether artificial intelligence (AI) will kill us all. Triggered by a spate of former workers at major AI firms coming forward to warn that a future superintelligent AI could lead to human extinction, the debate has inspired a kaleidoscopic array of views that don’t break down along neat ideological lines. Some think it’s all hogwash, either the product of ignorant hype or part of a cynical hype campaign by the industry itself. For others, convinced that the tech’s potential capabilities are no joke, they’re warnings that need to be taken deadly seriously.In many ways, though, the debate is besides the point. articles.title: Francis Fukuyama Is Welcoming History Back
articles.author: Matt McManus
articles.content_excerpt: In his new autobiography, Francis Fukuyama boasts that for decades “students in introductory classes in international relations all over the world were required to read [Samuel Huntington’s The Clash of Civilizations ] alongside The End of History .” The flex is warranted; during my undergrad we were assigned both essays in one of my classes on international law. Many intellectuals dream about reaching this level of notoriety. But for Fukuyama, fame came at a heavy price. Namely, he became the kind of thinker whose ideas everyone has an opinion on even while they resolutely avoid reading him (see 99 percent of recent conservative commentary on Karl Marx and Marxism for an example). articles.title: Cuba Under Siege
articles.content_excerpt: A ​ “ silent Gaza.” That is how a Cuban citizen summed up the impact of the U.S. decades-long blockade that the Trump administration has aggressively ratcheted up since the beginning of the year. In January, weeks after the military assault on Venezuela and the kidnapping of President Nicolás Maduro, Trump, invoking a ​ “ national emergency,” signed an executive order establishing punitive tariffs against any country that would provide Cuba with oil. Cuba depended on Venezuela for the largest share of its energy needs, in an ​ “ oil-for-doctors” agreement established in 2000 by Hugo Chávez and Fidel Castro. articles.title: Immigrants Aren't Taking Away Our Healthcare—ICE Is
articles.content_excerpt: The cost of healthcare just keeps going up — and millions of Americans are set to lose coverage. Under the GOP’s so-called ​ “ Big Beautiful Bill,” around 17 million people in this country will lose health care thanks to the law’s Medicaid cuts, failure to renew Affordable Care Act subsidies and other changes. Those cuts accelerate after this year’s midterms. Instead, that money is going toward tax cuts for the rich plus record budgets for Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Pentagon. Immigrants — including well over 1 million residents who are lawfully present — will be especially hard hit. articles.title: The Rising Left Can’t Ignore Labor’s Ongoing Crisis
articles.author: Sam Gindin
articles.content_excerpt: As the Trump administration stumbles from scandal to scandal and worries over artificial intelligence reach a fever pitch, there seems to be little relief in sight for working-class Americans confronting a stubborn cost-of-living crisis. The failure of both Republicans and Democrats to advance real solutions to the affordability crunch has opened the door to hopeful socialist election victories, including Zohran Mamdani’s triumph in New York last year and several left-wing wins in congressional primaries this summer. Yet organized labor by and large has continued its long retreat, and the prospects of significant national policy change still look remote. articles.title: A New Leader Wants to Move Bulgaria Left
articles.author: Krum Zarkov
articles.content_excerpt: Bulgaria might not be the first country you associate with the socialist movement. But left-wingers have played an outsize role in the southeastern European country, ever since some twenty activists founded the Bulgarian Social Democratic Workers’ Party at a clandestine mountain rendezvous in 1891. After the Russian Revolution, the newly formed Bulgarian Communist Party (BCP) launched a failed uprising in 1923, and, after playing a decisive role in the antifascist partisan resistance during World War II, took power with Soviet backing. Lasting from 1944 to 1990 and combining Soviet-style planning with nationalist policies that, over time, grew increasingly hostile toward the country’s Turkish minority, the BCP’s rule nevertheless fundamentally transformed Bulgaria. articles.title: What Cedric Robinson’s Black Marxism Gets Wrong
articles.author: August H. Nimtz
articles.content_excerpt: Cedric Robinson’s Black Marxism: The Making of the Black Radical Tradition did not receive widespread attention after its original publication in 1983. Since 2000, when it was republished with a new preface and an introduction by historian Robin D. G. Kelley, however, the book has enjoyed widespread appeal and influence in the anglophone humanities and social sciences as well as among activists. Robinson’s proposed theory of “racial capitalism” and his framework of a “black radical tradition” have shaped debates about racial inequalities in capitalist societies and Marxism’s potential for anti-racist politics in recent decades. articles.title: History From Below: Molly Crabapple’s Here Where We Live Is Our Country
articles.author: DSA Religion and Socialism Working Group
articles.content_excerpt: There is little new to say about Molly Crabapple’s wonderful history of the Jewish Bund , Here Where We Live is Our Country . Since its publication, the book has been widely celebrated by the Left, dismissed by the Right, and met with a mix of praise and accusations of naivety or idealism from liberal and centrist publications. The praise is well deserved. Crabapple writes so joyfully and tenderly about the Bund that a passive reading of the book feels almost heretical. The Bund was anti-Zionist, and Here Where We Live is Our Country is the kind of book that inspires people to continue the struggle against Zionism and genocide. articles.title: Socialists Should Be Champions of Government Efficiency
articles.author: Liza Featherstone
articles.content_excerpt: Early this week, Mayor Zohran Mamdani, speaking at the Urban 20 (U20) Mayors Summit, bemoaned that government “efficiency has been taken on as a right-wing concern,” with Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) being a particularly vile example. As with the phrase “quality of life,” the mayor observed, “there has been a sense that if you admit to an interest in those things, then you are assisting the Right.”On the contrary, the mayor said: “If you ignore these things,” that’s actually assisting the Right. articles.title: Amazon Workers Keep Walking Out
articles.content_excerpt: RIVERSIDE, CALIF. — In February, a worker at Amazon’s DJT 6 delivery station in Riverside was confronted inside the warehouse by a former coworker. She had accused him of harassment. The man had already been fired but somehow got back inside the building. Emmanuel Cadena, who works at DJT 6 and knew the woman, said the man blamed her for his firing. Another worker stepped in. “ He flashed the gun and said, ​ ‘ If you and your friend have a problem, you can see me outside,’” Cadena said. The confrontation happened near the conveyor belt where workers were sorting packages. Amazon did not pause work, according to Cadena. ​ “ There’s no sort of cover in any capacity,” he said.
